svg.title: blueprint card: service-memory-cap / svc_mem_cap_aggressive_steady_r1
svg.desc: service-memory-cap on run svc_mem_cap_aggressive_steady_r1 (sockshop): fires. The gap between the nearest other fault and this one is 1.59x. This run measured 4.59 x baseline on "time spent handling device interrupts"; the cut is at 2.00. The fault that comes closest to breaking this cut is code_serial_awaits on sockshop at 1.72. This number alone: 25 of 272 runs land on the wrong side. Every gate together: 253 of 272 runs correct. device interrupt time rose: pass (4.59 needs >= 2.00) and the disk stayed quiet: pass (62.6 needs <= 450.0) FIRED service-memory-cap - device interrupt time rose 4.59x with only 63 disk requests per unit of that rise - reclaim inside one cgroup, not the flood shape a disk fault gives no cpu-contention-co-tenant - None took 0.0 cores, but interrupt time is also raised with the disk quiet - that is a container against its memory limit whose stress tool happens to no db-latency-dependency-wait - the path is retransmitting 67.89% of segments across 1 interfaces - packets are being lost, so this is the network rather than the datastore no host-cpu-saturation - host CPU at 0.548, below the 0.95 ceiling no host-disk-saturation - disk arrivals per unit of interrupt rise 63, below the 450 bar no network-path-degradation - retransmission is 67.89% but nothing was dropped in the queue - the loss is happening in a receive buffer, not on the path, which is what an overloade no service-cpu-throttle - utilisation ratio 0.871, thief 0.0 cores, biggest loss -0.5507, runqueue 7.26x - not a quota holding work back
